title: Lender Preflight Coordination
name: Lender Preflight Coordination
metaTitle: Lender Preflight Coordination in Fort Worth, TX
metaDescription: Fort Worth 1031 exchange lender preflight coordination: aligning underwriting and closing timelines with the 180-day deadline across Alliance replacement deals.

sections.html: Financing a replacement property inside a 1031 exchange adds a lender timeline on top of the fixed 180-day deadline, and the two do not always move at the same speed. Fort Worth investors financing an Alliance industrial acquisition or a Southlake office building need lender preflight coordination to confirm underwriting can realistically finish before the exchange deadline rather than only before a standard closing date.

sections.heading: Starting Underwriting Before Identification Closes
sections.html:
Preflight coordination begins by engaging a lender during the identification window itself, using preliminary financials and a term sheet discussion to gauge underwriting timeline before a candidate property is locked in as the sole replacement. This matters most on properties near the defense corridor around the Lockheed campus, where lease structures tied to government-adjacent tenants can require additional lender review.

Getting ahead of underwriting also surfaces any loan-to-value or debt service coverage issue early enough to adjust the identification list if a candidate turns out to be difficult to finance on the intended timeline.

sections.heading: Aligning the Exchange Calendar With Lender Milestones
sections.html:
Once a lender is engaged, its underwriting milestones, appraisal, environmental review, and loan committee approval, are mapped against the 180-day deadline the same way title and escrow milestones are. On an Alliance-area industrial deal, appraisal turnaround for specialized rail-served buildings can run longer than a standard commercial appraisal, which preflight coordination accounts for early.

  • Confirm lender appraisal timeline against remaining exchange days
  • Verify environmental review requirements align with the closing date
  • Track loan committee approval milestones on the closing calendar
  • Coordinate final loan documents with the qualified intermediary's escrow instructions

sections.heading: Mortgage Boot Implications of Financing Terms
sections.html: The loan amount a lender ultimately approves affects mortgage boot calculations if it falls short of the debt relieved on the relinquished property, so preflight conversations with the lender include confirming likely loan-to-value terms early enough to plan for additional cash contribution if needed.

sections.heading: Contingency Planning for Financing Delays
sections.html: If lender underwriting risks slipping past the 180-day deadline, preflight coordination flags that risk early enough to consider an alternate identified candidate, additional cash in place of financing, or a renegotiated closing date with the seller, rather than discovering the conflict in the final weeks of the exchange.

sections.heading: Working With Lenders Familiar With Exchange Deadlines
sections.html:
Not every lender is equally comfortable underwriting against a fixed exchange deadline, and a loan officer accustomed to standard commercial closings may not treat day 180 with the same urgency an exchange requires. Preflight coordination includes confirming, early in the relationship, that the lender's team understands the deadline is not negotiable and can commit to a realistic closing date rather than a general target range.

On a Southlake or Colleyville acquisition where the lender is unfamiliar with exchange transactions, that conversation sometimes means walking through the mechanics of the qualified intermediary's role and the escrow structure so the lender's closing team does not introduce delay by requesting documentation or funding steps that conflict with how exchange proceeds actually move.

Confirming a lender's prior experience with exchange transactions before engaging them, rather than discovering unfamiliarity midway through underwriting, saves meaningful time. A lender who has closed similar 1031 transactions in the Fort Worth area typically has closing procedures already adapted to the qualified intermediary structure, which reduces the number of custom explanations and one-off accommodations the closing team has to negotiate under deadline pressure. Asking a prospective lender directly how many exchange transactions they have closed in the past year, and requesting a reference from a recent one, is a simple way to surface that experience before committing to the relationship. That upfront screening step is a small time investment relative to the risk of discovering, weeks into underwriting on an Alliance or Southlake acquisition, that a lender's process was never designed to accommodate a fixed statutory deadline in the first place. Adding that reference check to the standard lender-selection process gives the coordination team one more data point before committing to a financing partner on a deal where the closing date cannot move. That extra diligence step costs little time relative to the disruption a mid-underwriting lender swap would cause on a fixed exchange calendar.

faqs.q: When should a Fort Worth investor start talking to a lender in an exchange?
faqs.a: Lender conversations typically start during the 45-day identification window, using preliminary terms to confirm a candidate property can realistically be financed and closed before the 180-day deadline.

faqs.q: Does the 180-day deadline change based on financing complexity?
faqs.a: No. The statutory deadline is fixed regardless of how long lender underwriting takes, which is why preflight coordination focuses on fitting the lender's timeline into the existing deadline rather than assuming flexibility.

faqs.q: How does loan amount affect the exchange's tax treatment?
faqs.a: If the replacement loan amount is lower than the debt relieved on the relinquished property, the shortfall can create mortgage boot unless offset with additional cash, which investors should confirm with their tax advisor.

faqs.q: Can appraisal timelines on specialized industrial buildings affect the exchange deadline?
faqs.a: Yes. Appraisals on rail-served or specialized industrial buildings near Alliance can take longer than standard commercial appraisals, which is a common reason to start lender engagement early.

faqs.q: What happens if financing cannot close before day 180?
faqs.a: If financing cannot close in time, the investor may need to pursue an alternate identified property, bring additional cash to close without full financing, or accept that the exchange will fail if no replacement closes by the deadline.
